title.narrative: Empowered Tanzanian civil society for fostered justice & human rights in natural resource governance

description.narrative: - community representatives - civil society organisations (local, national and international) - small-scale miners’ associations, incl. the Tanzania Women Miners’ Association - trade unions - industry associations & businesses - local government authorities - ministries and governmental agencies - academics - Tanzanian Judiciary (Court of Appeal, High Court, and Subordinate)
Tanzanian communities and civil society organisations are empowered to engage government and industry in fostering access to justice, good governance and human rights in natural resource governance

This project aims to strengthen Tanzanian civil society organisations and communities with knowledge, skills, tools and opportunities to make sure that communities in Tanzania can benefit maximally from the extraction of natural resources (such as minerals and oil) while having to suffer the least harm possible from these extractive operations. In this way, Tanzania’s natural wealth can be a powerful driver of positive change and a way to improve the quality of life and overall wellbeing of Tanzania’s inhabitants, and not in the least its most disadvantaged ones.
To make sure people’s basic rights are better respected and protected, and their voices better heard by those in charge of business and policy decision-making, this project focusses on tackling three main stumbling blocks: (1) the limited understanding and poor documentation of the harms and benefits of natural resource extraction and the real-life negative and positive impacts on the people affected by the exploitation o...(+11 characters extra in FundHub text)

participating-org.narrative: Direction-Générale Coopération au Développement et Aide humanitaire

description.narrative: Result 1: Mapping and reporting of human rights issues and socio-economic impact related to natural resource governance by civil society organisations and those affected is improved

target.value: 1 dedicated digital platform for phone-based incident reporting & monitoring system is developed and operational.
1 dedicated digital platform is updated and operational following user feedback

baseline.value: CSOs generally have limited hands-on experience and capacity to gather, analyse and report community-based field-based human rights data linked to the impact of natural resource exploitation on communities, in a way that can be leveraged for the promotion

target.value: Staff from min. 12 CSOs show improved skills in human rights data gathering, analysis and reporting (as per mid-term survey). 50% of staff trained are women.
Staff from min. 16 CSOs show improved skills in human rights data gathering, analysis and reporting (as per final survey). 50% of staff trained are women

baseline.value: Evidence on issues related to justice, good governance and human rights in natural resource extraction is either not available or not easily accessible/digestible to a national and international public.

target.value: A digital central information hub on natural resource governance in Tanzania is developed and available online. Content is updated regularly. Min. 75% of output is (partially) made available in Kiswahili besides English.

A digital central information hub on natural resource governance in Tanzania is available online, updated regularly and fully maintained by Tanzanian project partners. Min. 75% of output is (partially) made available in Kiswahili besides English

baseline.value: Human rights issues in natural resource extraction and governance remain largely under-investigated and undocumented by field-based research and not accessible to an international audience

target.value: Min. 15 field-based case studies have been conducted. Min. 50% of cases specifically target issues faced by women and vulnerable groups.
Min. 20 field-based case studies have been conducted. Min. 50% of cases involve issues faced by women and vulnerable groups.

description.narrative: Result 2: Justice seekers are empowered to seek remedy for human rights abuses through improved corporate and government avenues

baseline.value: In many cases, justice seekers are not accompanied in their journey to seek remedy when faced with potential human rights violations. The baseline survey will collect data on justice seekers’ current satisfaction with the legal advice and/or support they

target.value: 60% of justice seekers state that they are satisfied with the legal advice and/or support provided (50% men, 50% women) (as per mid-term survey)
75% of justice seekers state that they are satisfied with the legal advice and/or support provided (50% men, 50% women) (as per final survey)

baseline.value: Justice seekers are generally unaware of how to access information on remedy in cases of human rights harm related to natural resource extraction. Baseline survey in targeted communities will inform the level of community awareness on accessing informatio

target.value: 60% of justice seekers from focal regions where public legal education interventions took place show increased awareness of access to information on human rights and access to remedy (50% men, 50% women) (as per mid-term survey)

75% of justice seekers from focal regions where public legal education interventions took place show increased awareness of access to information on human rights and access to remedy (50% men, 50% women) (as per final survey)

baseline.value: Often, legal actors do not have the tools and skills to support justice seekers to access remedy. A baseline survey will evaluate their capacity in a pre-test prior to engagement through the project.

target.value: Staff from 10 CSOs/ Legal Aid Service Providers (LASPs) show improved skills on legal assistance and representation (50% women) (as per mid-term survey)
Staff from 10 CSOs/LASPs show improved skills on legal strategies and representation (min. 50% women) (as per final survey)

baseline.value: followed-up in the to-be-developed incident reporting & monitoring system

target.value: 40% of incidents reported through the digital platform are followed up by civil society actors (case has been referred, taken up or a solution has been identified)
60% of incidents reported through the digital platform are followed up by civil society actors (case has been referred, taken up or a solution has been identified)

description.narrative: Result 3: Evidence-based multi-stakeholder dialogues promote corporate and governmental policy changes for improved justice, good governance and human rights in natural resource extraction

baseline.value: Between 2019 and 2020, 1 out of 5 sessions at annual national multi-stakeholder conferences on business and human rights in Tanzania, organized by IPIS, BHRT and CHRAGG, presented voices from local civil society organisations and communities

target.value: Local civil society and community actors (of which 50% women) actively present community perspectives in 25% of sessions at national and regional multi-stakeholder dialogues organized through the project

Local civil society and community actors (of which min. 50% women) actively present community perspectives in 35% of sessions at national and regional multi-stakeholder dialogues organized through the project

baseline.value: Capacity and awareness on human rights, justice and governance issues in the domain of natural resources is often not sufficient to guide policy decisions. A baseline survey will evaluate stakeholders’ capacity in a pre-test prior to engagement through th

target.value: 20 government and corporate stakeholders state that they have increased skills and know-how to base policy decisions on evidence-based policy advice developed through the project (as per mid-term survey).

30 government and corporate stakeholders state that they have increased skills and know-how to base policy decisions on evidence-based policy advice developed through the project (as per final survey).

baseline.value: Structural multi-stakeholder initiatives to formulate and discuss policy recommendations to improve access to justice, good governance and human rights in natural resources governance are absent.

target.value: Annually, 1-2 sets of policy recommendations are shared and developed at national and regional level multi-stakeholder dialogues organized through the project. Min. 20% of recommendations address issues specific to women and vulnerable groups.

Annually, min. two sets of policy recommendations are shared and developed at national and regional level multi-stakeholder dialogues organized through the project. Min. 30% of recommendations address issues specific to women and vulnerable groups.
